title: Marketplace Accessibility & Compliance Quickstart — EU & Healthcare Partners (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working quickstart for go-to-market, partner managers, and engineering/product touchpoints to accelerate marketplace listings for partners whose target customers include EU regional customers and healthcare verticals. Focus is two-fold: accessibility (WCAG/keyboard/ARIA) and regulated compliance (data residency, contracts, proofs).

Scope and audience:
- Audience: partner sales & enablement, listing ops, partner engineering, legal/compliance reviewers.
- Not a replacement for legal sign-off or SOC2/HIPAA documentation. It’s a pragmatic preflight to reduce back-and-forth during listing review.

High-level goals (what success looks like):
- Partner tile approved in marketplace within 7 business days for non-legal items, 14 for legal/regulatory reviews if artifacts are included up front.
- No accessibility-critical findings in the first marketplace QA pass (basic WCAG A/AA).
- EU customers see correct data residency copy and procurement artifacts linked.

Quick checklist (fast pass) — minimal required items partners must supply with listing request:
1) Tile copy + assets
   - Short tagline (<= 140 chars). One variant for EU audience if different wording required.
   - Long description (300–600 chars) with feature bullets and region-specific notes (data residency, certifications).
   - 1 hero screenshot, 1 architecture diagram (png). Note: architecture diagram must not include PII.
2) Compliance & residency
   - Data residency statement (yes/no) + supported regions (eu-west-1, eu-central-1 etc).
   - If processing is outside EU, provide lawful basis (SCCs/Model Clauses or equivalent).
   - Links to SOC2 report or attestation (PDF) or a SOC2 in-progress note with expected delivery.
   - If healthcare vertical: HIPAA/BAA status or equivalent regional healthcare compliance proof (or plan + timeline).
3) Technical integrations & SSO
   - SAML/OIDC support status and sample metadata file (or hosted IdP link).
   - KMS integration notes: customer-managed keys supported? KMS provider names.
4) Accessibility signoffs
   - WCAG checklist completed (A/AA) with owner name.
   - Keyboard nav verification: yes/no. Simple script/notes acceptable for first pass.
5) Service & SLA
   - Public SLA summary (uptime %, escalation email).
   - Contact for escalations and support flow (email + phone optional).
6) Pricing & procurement
   - Billing model (metered, seat, flat), sample invoice or SKU.

Accessibility (expanded):
- Required for listing: a one-page accessibility statement with owner and link to accessibility plan. Must declare WCAG conformance target and known exceptions.
- Quick tests to run before submission:
  - Axe or Lighthouse audit (attach report). Make sure no critical violations.
  - Keyboard-only navigation pass for tile & marketing pages (short video or list of tested pages).
  - Color contrast checks for hero and CTA buttons (attach screenshot with contrast ratios).
- For healthcare customers: emphasize content clarity, error messaging, and form input labels — accessibility issues often intersect with legal/regulatory risk.

Regulatory/Privacy & EU specifics:
- Data residency copy should be explicit. Example snippet: "Customer data is stored and processed in EU regions (eu-west-1, eu-central-1) unless explicitly configured otherwise; transfers outside the EU are governed by SCCs and documented in the DPA."
- Minimum artifacts for EU regulated customers: DPA (draft acceptable for first pass), SCC reference (if used), and a contact for data protection officer (or privacy lead).
- If partner uses subprocessors, list the top ones and whether they store customer content.

Healthcare vertical-specific notes:
- If partner is marketing to US healthcare customers, they must provide BAA/BAA roadmap (signed or in-progress expected).
- For non-US regulated healthcare (EU — e.g., GDPR + national health rules), provide privacy impact assessment if available.
- Minimum clinical risk statement: a short paragraph signed by product/engineering explaining how PHI is handled, retention, and de-identification practices.

Marketplace tile copy templates (scratch drafts) — vary by region and customer persona:
- Short tagline (tile): "Low-latency LLM inference with EU data residency and enterprise SLAs"
- Short EU-focused tagline: "LLM inference hosted in the EU — compliant and production-ready"
- Long description (partner-facing, concise): "[Partner] + Redwood Inference combine to deliver predictable, low-latency LLM inference with configurable EU data residency, KMS integrations, and enterprise SLAs. Ideal for regulated workloads in healthcare and finance. Try a 30-day trial."
- Callout bullets (for tile):
  - EU-region deployment options + DPA
  - HIPAA/BAA support (where applicable)
  - SOC2 Type II (or in progress)
  - SAML SSO and customer-managed keys

Sample acceptance gating rules (ops):
- Gate 1 (automated): tile assets present, required fields filled, hero image 1280x720 or larger.
- Gate 2 (accessibility): attached Lighthouse/Axe report with zero critical violations.
- Gate 3 (legal/compliance): DPA + data residency statement or explicit timeline for delivery. If healthcare marked, BAA present or timeline <= 30 days.
- Gate 4 (final): listing review by partner-program manager + one engineering review for SSO/KMS/integration claims.

Operational runbook (short):
1) Partner submits listing packet to partner-ops form (link: internal). Mark region tags (EU, Healthcare).
2) Automated QA runs: asset checks, basic copy checks, and accessibility report collection.
3) If failures: auto-generated feedback to partner with checklist items and examples.
4) If pass: schedule legal review (if EU or healthcare flagged). 48-hour SLA for legal triage if artifacts included.
5) Final QA & publish window: 24–48 hours after legal sign-off.

Unresolved questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Need a public copy snippet for "data residency vs data processing" that legal okays — short, non-technical.
- Confirm acceptable proof for SOC2 in progress — is a statement from auditor enough or do we require report PDF?
- Define minimal BAA roadmap template for partners who are close but not yet signed.
- Accessibility: who on product side is our final approver for WCAG claims? Ping @Avery.

Appendix: quick examples to paste into partner packet (editable)
- Data residency snippet (EU): "We process and store customer data in the EU by default. Where cross-border processing occurs, Standard Contractual Clauses are applied and documented in the Data Processing Addendum."
- Accessibility statement (short): "We aim for WCAG 2.1 AA compliance. Known exceptions: PDF docs in partner-upload flows; remediation plan in place. Accessibility contact: accessibility@partner.com"

Owners and contacts:
- Go-to-market owner: Jenna Lee (jenna@redwood.ai)
- Compliance/legal review: Priya Raman (priya@redwood.ai)
- Accessibility lead (product): Avery Chen (avery@redwood.ai)
- Technical review (SSO/KMS): Samir Patel (samir@redwood.ai)

Notes on tone and next steps:
- This doc is intentionally prescriptive (checklist-first) to reduce back-and-forth and speed time-to-publish.
- Next: convert to partner-facing checklist PDF and integrate into partner portal onboarding flow.
- Action: reach out to legal with the sample snippets (by 2025-02-20) and confirm acceptance criteria for "in-progress" artifacts.

End of draft.

(Working doc — feel free to paste into PRD or partner packet, but remember to replace [Partner] placeholders and remove internal comments before sharing externally.)
